title: Flatten PDF – Lock Form Fields and Comments Into the Page
description: Flatten a PDF in your browser: filled form fields and comments become part of the page, so they can't be changed and look the same anywhere. No upload.
heading: Flatten PDF
subtitle: Turn form fields and comments into part of the page, so the values can't be changed and look the same in every reader; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Flatten a PDF before you send a filled form or a reviewed document. Form fields and annotations (comments, highlights, stamps and drawings) are drawn into the page itself: the filled values stay visible, but nobody can type over them, and every reader shows them the same way. Arabic values are supported. The flattening happens in your browser, so your file never leaves your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your file is handled by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: Values locked
features.text: Filled fields become part of the page, so the answers can't be changed afterwards.

features.title: Same everywhere
features.text: Comments, highlights and stamps look the same in every PDF reader.

steps.title: Choose your PDF
steps.text: Click Choose a file, or drop a filled form or a reviewed PDF on the page.

steps.title: Check and download
steps.text: Check the preview and download the flattened copy; keep the original if you may need to edit it.

handles: Form fields: text boxes, check boxes, choices and their filled values.
Annotations: comments, highlights, stamps and drawings.
limits: Flattened fields can't be edited again, so keep the original file.
Some readers draw unusual fields differently, so check the preview before you send the copy.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your file is read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: How do I flatten a PDF form so it can't be edited?
faq.answer: Flattening draws a form's fields and their values into the page, so they show as ordinary content that can't be typed over. Here, choose the filled PDF, click Flatten PDF and download the copy, all in your browser.

faq.question: Do the values I filled in stay visible?
faq.answer: Yes. Every filled value is drawn on the page where its field was, Arabic included; only the field around it is removed.

faq.question: Can I edit the fields after flattening?
faq.answer: No. That is the point of flattening, so keep the original if you may need to change an answer. You can fill it again with Fill PDF form, then flatten a new copy.

faq.question: Why does a field look different after flattening?
faq.answer: PDF readers draw some unusual fields in their own way, and the flattened copy keeps one fixed look. Check the preview before you send it.

faq.question: Does flattening hide what is under a comment?
faq.answer: No. Flattening only draws the comments into the page; the text under them stays in the file. To remove text for good, use Redact PDF.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.
